claims.claim: Photius was patriarch of Constantinople from 858 to 866 and from 877 to 886 CE.
Photius was a leading figure of the 9th-century Byzantine renascence.
Prior to his installation as patriarch, Photius served as the head of the University of Constantinople.
The extracts associated with Photius in the catenae are generally marked with a siglum consisting of a τ with an elongated vertical bar which intersects with a φ and an ω at the base.
Photius is the latest (dated) commentator to be added to the standard collection of patristic authors.
The Fragmenta in epistulam ad Philippenses survives in catenae (chain-commentaries).
The work is included in Migne's Patrologia Graeca, volumes CI-CV.
Manuscripts containing the Fragmenta in epistulas S. Pauli include Vatican, Biblioteca apostolica vaticana, Ott.gr.356 and Venice, Biblioteca nazionale Marciana, MS gr. II. 15 (coll. 1090).
